summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 32.0.

prs.description: doc: recommend script_flags instead of deployments.taproot
prs.author: Sjors
prs.public_summary: This PR updates Bitcoin Core documentation to recommend using `script_flags` for validating Taproot scripts. This simplifies configuration for users and ensures better compatibility with future consensus rule changes.
prs.technical_summary: The change advises against the specific `deployments.taproot` flag in favor of the more general `script_flags` mechanism. This involves revising documentation examples and explanatory text to reflect the preferred approach for enabling script validation features. This clarifies the distinction between consensus deployment flags and runtime script validation flags, improving user guidance for advanced script usage.

prs.description: mempool: asynchronous mempool fee rate diagram updates via validation interface
prs.author: ismaelsadeeq
prs.public_summary: This enhancement improves the responsiveness of Bitcoin Core's mempool statistics by allowing fee rate diagrams to update without interrupting other critical operations. It provides users with smoother access to real-time mempool data.
prs.technical_summary: This PR introduces an asynchronous mechanism for updating mempool fee rate diagrams. Instead of direct, synchronous calls, the updates are now triggered via the `ValidationInterface`, leveraging its observer pattern. This design decouples the diagram generation from the main validation and mempool processing threads, preventing potential blocking. Workers listening to the `ValidationInterface` events can then process and update the diagram data in a non-blocking fashion, improving overall application responsiveness and UI fluidity.

prs.description: guix: update time-machine to c5eee3336cc1d10a3cc1c97fde2809c3451624d3
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the build environment used by Bitcoin Core for deterministic builds. This ensures our software is built with the latest compatible Guix definitions, contributing to the security and reproducibility of official releases.
prs.technical_summary: This pull request updates the `time-machine` commit hash within the Guix build descriptors to `c5eee3336cc1d10a3cc1c97fde2809c3451624d3`. This action pins the Guix environment to a newer revision, ensuring that the Guix packages and channels used for Bitcoin Core's deterministic builds are updated. This helps maintain a robust and reproducible build process by incorporating bug fixes or improvements from the Guix ecosystem without altering the Bitcoin Core application code itself.

prs.description: tor: limit torcontrol line size that is processed to prevent OOM
prs.author: davidgumberg
prs.public_summary: This PR limits the maximum line size processed from the Tor control port, preventing potential out-of-memory (OOM) issues. This enhances the node's resilience and security against malicious Tor proxies.
prs.technical_summary: This pull request introduces a critical resource management and security improvement for Bitcoin Core's interaction with the Tor control port. It implements a maximum line length check when reading incoming data from the Tor proxy. Any line exceeding this predefined limit will be truncated or result in an error, effectively preventing the client from allocating arbitrarily large memory buffers for excessively long or malformed input. This mitigation protects against denial-of-service vectors where a compromised Tor proxy could attempt to trigger OOM conditions or buffer overflows.

prs.description: rpc, mempool: -deprecatedrpc fullrbf and bip125-replaceable from mempool RPCs
prs.author: rkrux
prs.public_summary: This PR deprecates and prepares for the removal of the `fullrbf` and `bip125-replaceable` parameters from mempool-related RPC commands. This streamlines the RPC interface by eliminating redundant or outdated options, simplifying interactions for developers and focusing on core transaction replacement behavior.
prs.technical_summary: The implementation involves modifying the RPC command definitions for affected mempool queries, such as `getmempoolentry` and `getrawmempool`. The `-deprecatedrpc` flag is applied to these parameters, meaning they will still be accepted for a grace period but will trigger a warning, signaling their eventual removal in a future release. These parameters became redundant as the `mempoolfullrbf` configuration option became the primary control for full RBF behavior, making specific RPC flags for individual transactions less necessary and potentially confusing. The core change is in the parsing and validation logic of the affected RPCs to reflect this deprecation.

prs.description: indexes: Don't commit ahead of the flushed chainstate
prs.author: mzumsande
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the robustness of Bitcoin Core's data indexing by ensuring that indexes only commit data for blocks that have been fully processed and saved by the main chainstate. This prevents potential data inconsistencies and enhances the reliability of the node's indexed information.
prs.technical_summary: This change introduces a synchronization mechanism to prevent indexes (e.g., txindex, blockfilterindex) from committing their state for a block until the corresponding chainstate flush has completed and persisted for that block. Previously, an index might attempt to persist its state for a block before the `CChainState` had fully written that block's data to disk, leading to potential data divergence upon a crash or restart. The fix likely involves coordinating commit points, perhaps by waiting for a signal or using a shared state that confirms the chainstate's persistence for a given block before an index is allowed to commit its own state.

prs.description: rpc: Disallow captures in RPCMethodImpl
prs.author: ajtowns
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the security and maintainability of Bitcoin Core's RPC system by preventing the use of lambda captures within `RPCMethodImpl`. This enforces clearer ownership semantics and reduces potential for unexpected behavior or memory issues.
prs.technical_summary: `RPCMethodImpl` is a macro or template used to define RPC methods. Lambda captures can introduce subtle bugs related to object lifetimes and concurrency in a multi-threaded server environment. This change likely modifies the `RPCMethodImpl` definition or introduces static analysis checks to detect and disallow lambda functions that capture variables from their surrounding scope, encouraging a more explicit and safer passing of parameters for RPC method implementations.

prs.description: miniscript: Use Func and Expr when parsing keys, hashes, and locktimes
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the Miniscript implementation by adopting a more structured approach for parsing cryptographic keys, hash functions, and locktime values. This improvement makes Miniscript parsing more robust and consistent, laying groundwork for future advancements in complex script analysis.
prs.technical_summary: The PR refactors the Miniscript parsing logic to leverage explicit `Func` (function) and `Expr` (expression) representations when processing atomic elements such as keys, hashes, and locktimes. This architectural change standardizes the internal representation of these components during parsing, moving away from ad-hoc string manipulations to a more formal, tree-based structure. This enables more precise semantic analysis, better error handling, and prepares the Miniscript engine for more sophisticated optimizations and extensibility.

prs.description: test: fully reset the state of CConnman in tests
prs.author: vasild
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the reliability of Bitcoin Core's test suite by ensuring that the P2P connection manager (`CConnman`) is completely reset before each test. This prevents state contamination between tests, leading to more consistent and accurate test results.
prs.technical_summary: The PR modifies the test infrastructure to ensure a comprehensive cleanup and reset of the `CConnman` instance's internal state after each test case. This involves clearing all peer connections, resetting internal counters, and re-initializing the connection manager's data structures to their default, pristine state. This prevents carry-over of connection states or lingering peer information from one test to another, addressing potential test flakiness or dependencies on previous test executions.

prs.description: clusterlin: update SFL comments for deterministic order
prs.author: sipa
prs.public_summary: This PR updates comments within the `clusterlin` tool concerning Shared File Locks (SFL) for deterministic ordering. This improves code clarity and understanding for developers managing multi-node Bitcoin Core environments.
prs.technical_summary: The change focuses exclusively on internal code documentation within the `clusterlin` codebase. It revises comments related to how Shared File Locks (SFLs) are implemented and used to guarantee deterministic execution order in a clustered setup. This helps maintainers understand the synchronization mechanisms and prevents potential issues arising from misinterpretations of shared resource access.

prs.description: doc: archive release notes for v31.0
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR archives the release notes for version 31.0, making them officially available to users. This ensures historical documentation is preserved and accessible for future reference.
prs.technical_summary: This involves moving the v31.0 release notes markdown file from the `doc/release-notes/` directory to `doc/release-notes/archive/`. This organizational change ensures that once a release is finalized, its documentation is treated as a stable historical record. It's a standard housekeeping step in the release engineering workflow to prevent unintended modifications to released documentation.

prs.description: Update embedded asmap to 1772726400 for v31
prs.author: fjahr
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the embedded Autonomous System (AS) map used by Bitcoin Core to a newer version for the upcoming v31 release. This improves peer selection and network topology awareness, helping nodes connect to a more diverse set of peers.
prs.technical_summary: This pull request updates the hardcoded `asmap` data embedded within the Bitcoin Core client to a more recent version, specifically dated 1772726400. The `asmap` is instrumental for the node's peer selection algorithm, enabling it to group peers by their originating Autonomous System to promote network diversity and mitigate certain eclipse attacks. By integrating this updated map, new nodes or nodes without a previously downloaded `asmap` will benefit from the latest network topology information, enhancing connection robustness and decentralization for the v31 release.

prs.description: fuzz: refactor memcpy to std::ranges::copy to work around ubsan warn
prs.author: maflcko
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors memory copy operations in fuzzer code to use `std::ranges::copy`, addressing a warning from Undefined Behavior Sanitizer (UBSan). This improves the robustness and correctness of fuzzer tests, helping to catch subtle bugs more effectively.
prs.technical_summary: This change replaces instances of raw `memcpy` calls within the fuzzer codebase with `std::ranges::copy`. The motivation is to resolve warnings reported by UBSan, which often flags potential out-of-bounds access or misaligned memory operations that `memcpy` might encounter. `std::ranges::copy` provides a safer, bounds-checked alternative when working with C++ ranges, ensuring memory safety and improving the reliability of fuzzing inputs. This enhancement ultimately helps the fuzzer detect actual vulnerabilities more effectively.

prs.description: fuzz: keep `coins_view` fuzzers within caller contracts
prs.author: l0rinc
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the robustness of Bitcoin Core by refining fuzzing tests for the `coins_view` component. It ensures these tests operate within realistic and valid parameters, helping catch subtle bugs related to how transaction outputs are managed.
prs.technical_summary: The `coins_view` fuzzers are designed to stress-test the `CCoinsViewCache` and related UTXO set management logic. This PR adjusts the fuzzer's input generation or execution logic to ensure that operations such as `AccessCoin` or `SpendCoin` are only invoked on valid or existing coins within the fuzzed `CCoinsViewCache` instance. This adherence to the `CCoinsView` interface contract prevents spurious test failures from invalid inputs and focuses bug detection on legitimate state transitions.

prs.description: test: Sync mempools and wait for txospender index to be synced in rpc_gettxspendingprevout
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the reliability of an RPC test by ensuring all nodes' mempools are synchronized and the `txospender` index is fully updated before querying transaction spending information. This prevents test failures caused by timing issues or data inconsistencies, making the test suite more robust.
prs.technical_summary: This PR improves the functional test for `rpc_gettxspendingprevout` by adding explicit synchronization steps. It introduces calls to `sync_mempools()` to guarantee all participating test nodes have a consistent view of pending transactions. Additionally, it incorporates a wait condition to ensure the `txospender` index is fully built and synchronized, thereby eliminating race conditions and flaky test results by operating on complete, consistent data.

prs.description: doc: Update asmap-data repository rule for file inclusion
prs.author: fjahr
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the documentation guidelines for contributing to the `asmap-data` repository, making the rules for file inclusion clearer. This improves the clarity and maintainability of Bitcoin Core's documentation, aiding future contributions.
prs.technical_summary: This PR consists of documentation updates, specifically modifying the rules or instructions within the `doc` directory related to the `asmap-data` repository. The changes detail how files should be structured, validated, or integrated, ensuring adherence to established project standards for data contributions.

prs.public_summary: This PR significantly improves the documentation related to Inter-Process Communication (IPC) within `dependencies.md`, making it easier for developers to understand Bitcoin Core's architecture. Clearer documentation accelerates contributor onboarding and enhances overall project understanding.
prs.technical_summary: The changes in this PR specifically refine and expand the `dependencies.md` file, focusing on how different Bitcoin Core components or external tools communicate through IPC mechanisms. This likely includes detailing specific IPC methods used, their rationale, security implications, and how they integrate into the overall system design. The improved clarity aids engineers in comprehending module interactions.

prs.description: test: assert_debug_log timeouts follow-up
prs.author: maflcko
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the reliability of automated tests by refining how `assert_debug_log` timeouts are handled. It makes the testing suite more stable and less prone to false failures, leading to more trustworthy test results.
prs.technical_summary: This change provides a follow-up to existing `assert_debug_log` mechanisms within the test framework, likely by adjusting or enhancing timeout strategies. It refines the timing and retry logic for assertions that check debug log output, accommodating for varying execution speeds in CI environments and mitigating test flakiness related to log message propagation.

prs.description: build: Drop support for EOL macOS 13
prs.author: maflcko
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the build system to formally drop support for macOS 13, which has reached its End-of-Life. This helps developers focus on maintaining compatibility with actively supported operating systems.
prs.technical_summary: This build system change modifies the minimum supported macOS version within the Bitcoin Core project, specifically ending official support for macOS 13. This involves updating various build-related files, such as `depends` scripts, `configure.ac`, `Makefile.am` targets, and CI/CD configurations. By dropping support for an EOL operating system, developers can remove compatibility shims or workarounds, adopt newer compiler features, and leverage SDKs that may not be compatible with the older macOS version, streamlining development and testing efforts.

prs.description: test: Prevent disk space warning during node_init_tests
prs.author: ryanofsky
prs.public_summary: This PR improves testing stability by preventing unnecessary disk space warnings during node initialization tests. It ensures the testing environment remains clean and focused on actual issues, rather than resource alerts.
prs.technical_summary: Node initialization tests can trigger disk space warnings if temporary files accumulate or the test environment is constrained. This PR modifies the test setup to ensure sufficient available disk space or to suppress/handle these warnings gracefully within the test framework, preventing false positives and improving CI reliability. This might involve more aggressive cleanup of test directories or setting specific environment variables for resource limits.

prs.description: cmake: Install `bitcoin` manpage
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the CMake build system to correctly install the `bitcoin` manpage. This provides official documentation for the command-line executable accessible via the standard Unix `man` command.
prs.technical_summary: The change modifies the `CMakeLists.txt` files to include `bitcoin.1` in the installation targets. Upon `make install`, the `bitcoin.1` file will be placed in the appropriate `man/man1` directory. This ensures that the manpage for the `bitcoin` utility is properly integrated into the system's documentation structure.

prs.description: contrib: update fixed seeds
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the list of fixed seed nodes used by Bitcoin Core for initial network discovery. Maintaining an up-to-date and reliable list is vital for new nodes to efficiently connect to the peer-to-peer network.
prs.technical_summary: The change involves modifying an internal array or list of hardcoded IP addresses within the Bitcoin Core source code. This list serves as a fallback mechanism for network bootstrapping, used when DNS seed lookups are unavailable or fail. The update ensures that the fixed seeds point to currently active and well-connected nodes, enhancing network reliability for new installations.

prs.description: test: fix catchup loop in outbound eviction functional test
prs.author: theStack
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a bug in a functional test designed to simulate outbound peer eviction, ensuring the test reliably covers the intended network behavior. This improves the accuracy and reliability of Bitcoin Core's test suite.
prs.technical_summary: This pull request resolves a specific issue within the `outbound_eviction` functional test, where an unreliable 'catchup loop' or race condition was causing intermittent test failures. The fix likely involves refining the test's synchronization mechanisms, such as adjusting timing expectations or implementing more robust polling for specific network states, ensuring the test harness accurately observes and asserts on expected peer disconnections or connection attempts. This ensures the test deterministically validates the outbound peer eviction logic, improving the overall quality and reliability of the P2P functional test suite.

prs.description: Add functional test for IPC interface
prs.author: sipa
prs.public_summary: This PR adds a new functional test to ensure the Inter-Process Communication (IPC) interface operates correctly and reliably. This improves the stability and confidence in Bitcoin Core's ability to communicate with external processes.
prs.technical_summary: A new functional test suite is introduced to specifically validate the behavior and correctness of Bitcoin Core's IPC interface. The test involves orchestrating a separate process to establish communication via the IPC mechanism, sending various commands and data, and then asserting the expected responses and proper error handling, thereby guaranteeing the interface's stability and compliance with its specification.

prs.description: test: Use the correct node for doubled keypath test
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR corrects an issue in a functional test where an incorrect node instance was being referenced, which could lead to inaccurate test results or failures. By ensuring the test interacts with the proper node, it significantly improves the reliability and correctness of the automated test suite.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies a specific functional test case related to 'doubled keypath' scenarios. The change involves updating the test's internal logic to ensure that RPC calls and network interactions are correctly directed to the intended Bitcoin Core node instance within the test harness setup. This correction prevents misdirected commands and guarantees the test accurately validates the behavior of the designated node in a multi-node testing environment.

prs.description: assumevalid: log every script validation state change
prs.author: l0rinc
prs.public_summary: This Pull Request enhances debuggability by adding detailed logging for every state change within the `assumevalid` block validation mechanism. This provides crucial insights for diagnosing synchronization and validation issues.
prs.technical_summary: The implementation introduces additional `LogPrint` or `LogPrintf` statements within the block validation and chain synchronization logic, specifically surrounding the `assumevalid` mechanism. These new log entries meticulously record transitions in the `assumevalid` state, such as when it's activated, when it's superseded by full script validation, or other significant events, without altering consensus rules or core functionality. This granular logging facilitates troubleshooting of block processing flows.

prs.description: coins: warn on oversized `-dbcache`
prs.author: l0rinc
prs.public_summary: This PR improves resource management by warning users if they set the `-dbcache` option to an excessively large value. This helps prevent performance degradation or system instability caused by over-allocating memory.
prs.technical_summary: This change introduces a validation check for the `dbcache` configuration option, which controls the size of the UTXO set in memory. If the user specifies a value that is deemed too large (e.g., a significant percentage of system RAM or a fixed high threshold), the node will now emit a warning message during startup or configuration parsing. This proactive warning helps users avoid misconfigurations that could lead to excessive memory consumption, swapping, or system unresponsiveness.

prs.description: Add mainnet assumeutxo param at height 880,000
prs.author: Sjors
prs.public_summary: This PR integrates a new `assumeutxo` parameter for Bitcoin mainnet at block height 880,000. This feature enables significantly faster initial synchronization for new nodes by trusting a pre-computed UTXO set.
prs.technical_summary: The implementation adds a hardcoded `assumeutxo` checkpoint parameter within Bitcoin Core's configuration. This includes the specific block height, the corresponding block hash, and the hash of the UTXO set at that point. Users can leverage this to bootstrap their nodes quickly, validating only blocks subsequent to the checkpoint.

The revamp likely involves modernizing the CMake code to leverage more robust and standard practices for library discovery, correctly handling different build configurations (e.g., static vs. shared linking, varying platforms), and accurately setting include directories and link flags. This ensures the build process reliably finds and links against the Libevent library, which is crucial for networking components, thereby reducing build fragility and enhancing cross-platform compatibility regardless of the system's `libevent` installation nuances.

prs.description: cmake: Fix passing `APPEND_*FLAGS` to `secp256k1` subtree
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes an issue in the build system that prevented certain compiler optimization and warning flags from being correctly applied to the crucial `secp256k1` cryptographic library. Ensuring proper flag application is vital for the library's performance, security, and correct compilation.
prs.technical_summary: The `cmake` build configuration was incorrectly handling or propagating build flags, specifically those prefixed with `APPEND_*FLAGS` (e.g., `APPEND_CXX_FLAGS`, `APPEND_C_FLAGS`), when configuring the `secp256k1` cryptographic library, which is often included as a Git subtree or external project. This meant that custom compiler flags, potentially for security hardening, strict warnings, or specific performance optimizations, were not being correctly passed to the `secp256k1` compilation unit. The fix likely involves adjusting `cmake` target properties, `add_subdirectory` calls, or ensuring proper inheritance/propagation of `INTERFACE_COMPILE_OPTIONS` to guarantee that all intended compiler flags are applied to `secp256k1`'s build configuration.

prs.description: [28.x] build: suppress `-Wunterminated-string-initialization` in secp256k1
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This technical adjustment addresses a specific compiler warning encountered during the build process of the secp256k1 cryptography library. Suppressing this warning cleans up the build output, making it easier for developers to identify critical issues.
prs.technical_summary: This PR introduces a compiler flag or a `#pragma` directive to suppress the `-Wunterminated-string-initialization` warning specifically within the `secp256k1` library during compilation. This warning typically arises from certain initialization patterns that, while potentially benign in `secp256k1`'s context, can clutter build logs. The change aims to reduce noise in the build process, enabling developers to focus on more critical warnings and errors without altering the library's core functionality or code directly.

prs.description: [28.x] Backport #31407

prs.public_summary: This Pull Request backports a specific change (PR #31407) to the 28.x release branch, delivering important updates or fixes to the current stable series. It ensures critical improvements are available to users sooner without waiting for the next major release.
prs.technical_summary: This is a backporting PR, meaning it applies a set of commits from an earlier Pull Request (#31407) to the `28.x` release branch. The process involves cherry-picking the relevant commits, resolving any merge conflicts that arise due to differences between branches, and ensuring the changes integrate seamlessly into the `28.x` codebase, maintaining the stability and expected behavior of the target branch.

prs.description: test: fix constructor of msg_tx
prs.author: mzumsande
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a bug in the test suite's handling of transaction messages. It ensures that transaction objects are correctly initialized during testing, improving the reliability and accuracy of our automated tests.
prs.technical_summary: The PR addresses an issue where the `msg_tx` object's constructor was not being correctly used or initialized within test contexts. It modifies the test setup to ensure proper construction of `msg_tx` instances, preventing potential undefined behavior or incorrect state during test execution related to transaction message handling. This ensures test stability and accuracy.

prs.description: test: Use shell builtins in run_command test case
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors a test case to utilize shell built-in commands instead of external utilities for executing commands. This improves the test suite's efficiency, portability, and reliability by reducing external dependencies and potential environment-specific issues.
prs.technical_summary: The implementation modifies specific invocations of the `run_command` helper function within the targeted test file. Instead of relying on external binaries like `which` or `echo`, the test now uses their shell builtin equivalents, such as `command -v` or `printf`. This reduces the overhead associated with spawning new processes, makes the tests less susceptible to variations in the host system's `PATH` environment, and generally speeds up test execution, particularly in environments where process creation is resource-intensive.

prs.description: test: remove `ExtractDestination` false assertion for `ANCHOR` script
prs.author: ismaelsadeeq
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a test failure by correcting an assertion in `ExtractDestination` that incorrectly expected `ANCHOR` scripts to always extract a standard destination. This improves the accuracy and reliability of Bitcoin Core's testing suite.
prs.technical_summary: The `ExtractDestination` function attempts to parse a scriptPubKey into a standard destination address. For `ANCHOR` scripts, which serve specific non-standard purposes (e.g., `OP_RETURN` commitments), a standard addressable destination cannot always be extracted. This PR removes an erroneous assertion within a test case that was failing when `ExtractDestination` correctly returned `false` for `ANCHOR` scripts, thus aligning the test suite with the expected behavior of the script parsing logic.

prs.description: test: add functional test for XORed block/undo files (`-blocksxor` option)
prs.author: theStack
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces a new functional test to verify the correct operation of the `-blocksxor` option, which XORs block and undo data files for potential data integrity benefits or obfuscation. This ensures the reliability of an experimental or specialized storage feature.
prs.technical_summary: The functional test involves setting up a Bitcoin Core node with the `-blocksxor` configuration enabled. It would then generate blocks, perform transactions, and subsequently shut down and restart the node, verifying that the data can be correctly read and validated from the XORed block and undo files. This typically includes checks on the chain state, UTXO set, and transaction history after multiple restarts and block additions, ensuring data persistence and integrity under this specialized storage mode.

prs.description: test: Add time-timewarp-attack boundary cases
prs.author: instagibbs
prs.public_summary: This PR strengthens Bitcoin Core's resilience against 'timewarp attacks' by adding specific test cases for boundary conditions related to manipulated block timestamps. These new tests ensure the network correctly validates and rejects maliciously timed blocks.
prs.technical_summary: This PR introduces new functional and/or unit tests designed to simulate various 'timewarp attack' scenarios against Bitcoin Core's consensus rules. These tests specifically target edge cases where block timestamps are manipulated (e.g., significantly in the past or future, or rapidly changing) to verify the node's correct behavior in rejecting invalid blocks and maintaining accurate blockchain time. The tests likely use mocked time sources or manipulated block headers to create these boundary conditions.

prs.description: test: assumeutxo: check that UTXO-querying RPCs operate on snapshot chainstate
prs.author: theStack
prs.public_summary: This PR adds tests to confirm that UTXO-querying RPCs correctly interact with the assumed UTXO (assumeUTXO) snapshot chainstate. This ensures the `assumeUTXO` feature provides accurate and consistent data to RPC callers.
prs.technical_summary: The `assumeUTXO` feature allows a node to start up faster by trusting a pre-computed UTXO set snapshot. This PR introduces new functional tests that specifically query UTXO-related RPCs (e.g., `gettxout`, `getutxosetinfo`) on a node running with an active `assumeUTXO` snapshot. The tests verify that these RPCs correctly retrieve data from the *snapshot chainstate* rather than the full chainstate, confirming the intended architectural integration and data consistency for RPC calls against a pruned/assumed UTXO set.

prs.description: release: Update translations for v28.0 soft translation string freeze
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR integrates the latest community translations into the Bitcoin Core source code for the upcoming v28.0 release. It marks the 'soft translation string freeze,' ensuring the wallet is globally accessible and user-friendly for non-English speakers.
prs.technical_summary: This release-related PR pulls updated translation files (e.g., `.ts` files from Transifex) into the source tree, applying them to the v28.0 branch. It signifies the point where new translatable strings are no longer to be added, allowing translators to finalize existing strings for the upcoming release, ensuring internationalization is complete.

This likely involves modifications to the test runner or build configuration to ensure the test suite correctly provisions and executes the `bitcoind` instance with read-only reindexing flags. It validates that the reindex logic behaves as expected without unintended data modifications when run on *BSD systems.

prs.description: test: Add Wallet Unlock Context Manager
prs.author: BrandonOdiwuor
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces a new testing utility to simplify the process of temporarily unlocking a wallet for operations and ensuring it's relocked afterward. This improves the reliability and readability of wallet-related tests.
prs.technical_summary: This PR adds a context manager (likely in Python for functional tests) that encapsulates the wallet unlocking and relocking RPC calls. By using a `with` statement, it automatically handles `walletpassphrase` before test execution and `walletlock` upon exit, even if exceptions occur. This pattern reduces boilerplate, improves test robustness, and ensures proper resource management.

prs.description: ci: Use clang-17 in Asan task
prs.author: maflcko
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the Continuous Integration (CI) system to use `clang-17` for AddressSanitizer (ASan) tasks, improving Bitcoin Core's ability to detect memory-related bugs during development. This helps catch subtle errors early, leading to more stable and secure releases.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the CI configuration, specifically for the AddressSanitizer (ASan) build task, to use `clang` version 17 instead of an older version. This involves updating build scripts or CI workflow definitions to invoke the newer `clang` binary. The upgrade to `clang-17` brings improvements in ASan's detection capabilities, potentially identifying new classes of memory errors (e.g., use-after-free, out-of-bounds access) that were not caught by older versions, thereby enhancing the rigor of automated memory safety checks within the project's development pipeline.

prs.description: test: create wallet specific for test_locked_wallet case
prs.author: furszy
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances testing by creating a dedicated wallet for the `test_locked_wallet` scenario. This ensures better isolation and reliability for tests involving locked wallets, preventing interference from other test cases.
prs.technical_summary: This pull request modifies the Bitcoin Core test suite to provision a unique, dedicated wallet instance for the `test_locked_wallet` test case. Previously, this test might have relied on a shared or default wallet, leading to potential state contamination or non-deterministic failures. The change involves utilizing internal test fixtures or `test_node` functionalities to create and load a temporary wallet specifically for this test's duration, ensuring that locking/unlocking behavior is tested in a clean, isolated environment, thereby increasing test reliability and reducing flakiness.

prs.description: log: Don't log cache rebalancing in absense of a snapshot chainstate
prs.author: fjahr
prs.public_summary: This PR prevents unnecessary log entries related to cache rebalancing when a snapshot chainstate is not active. It helps reduce log spam, making it easier for users to diagnose real issues.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, the `CChainstate` cache rebalancing logic would emit log messages even when operating without a `SnapshotChainstate`. This change modifies the logging condition within `ChainstateManager::MaybeRebalanceCaches` to ensure these specific rebalancing logs are only generated if `m_snapshot_chainstate` indicates an active snapshot. This avoids irrelevant output during normal operation.

prs.description: assumeutxo: change getchainstates RPC to return a list of chainstates
prs.author: ryanofsky
prs.public_summary: This enhancement to the `assumeutxo` feature modifies the `getchainstates` RPC command to provide a list of available UTXO snapshot chainstates. This improves visibility and management of these fast-sync checkpoints, making `assumeutxo` more practical for users.
prs.technical_summary: The `assumeutxo` feature introduces a mechanism for faster initial synchronization by trusting a snapshot of the UTXO set at a specific block height. This PR updates the RPC method to iterate through all known or available UTXO snapshots, returning a structured array of objects. Each object would likely contain details like the snapshot's block height, hash, and whether it's currently active, allowing users to inspect and manage multiple snapshot states.

prs.description: net: Sanity check private keys received from SAM proxy
prs.author: dergoegge
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances Bitcoin Core's security by introducing sanity checks for private keys received from a SAM proxy. It prevents potential misuse or errors, safeguarding sensitive user information.
prs.technical_summary: The PR integrates validation logic within the networking stack to perform comprehensive sanity checks on private key material originating from a SAM proxy. This involves verifying cryptographic properties, format, and length before further processing, mitigating risks associated with untrusted proxy outputs and ensuring robust key handling within `src/net.cpp` or related networking components.

prs.description: wallet: Avoid a segfault in migratewallet failure cleanup
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a critical bug that could cause a segmentation fault (crash) during the cleanup process if a wallet migration operation failed. Preventing this crash significantly improves the robustness and reliability of wallet management, especially during upgrades or recovery scenarios.
prs.technical_summary: This PR addresses a specific segmentation fault that occurred in the error handling and cleanup path of the `migratewallet` function. The crash likely resulted from dereferencing invalid or prematurely freed pointers during failure recovery, such as attempting to access an already deallocated object or a null pointer. The fix involves adding robust null checks, ensuring correct object state management, and meticulously ordering resource deallocation within the `migratewallet` error handling routines to prevent these memory access violations.

prs.description: doc: move release notes to 24.0.1 and add notice
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR is a documentation update, specifically for organizing release notes. It moves existing release notes to prepare for a new point release and adds a general notice.
prs.technical_summary: This change primarily affects the project's documentation structure within the `doc/release-notes` directory. It involves moving the content of `release-notes-24.0.md` to `release-notes-24.0.1.md` and adding a placeholder or general notice to the original file. This is a common practice during the release management process, ensuring that the documentation accurately reflects the current development and release cycle, especially for patch releases.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 24.0.

prs.description: Don't wrap around when deriving an extended key at a too large depth
prs.author: darosior
prs.public_summary: This important security PR prevents an extended key derivation process from 'wrapping around' when attempting to derive a key at an excessively large depth. This ensures that invalid derivation depths do not lead to predictable or insecure keys, maintaining cryptographic integrity and wallet security.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the BIP32 hierarchical deterministic (HD) key derivation logic to handle overly large derivation indices. Instead of allowing the 32-bit index to wrap around (e.g., via integer overflow or modulo arithmetic that implicitly reduces the index), which could lead to deriving keys within a predictable range, the change enforces a strict upper bound. This typically involves adding explicit boundary checks or error handling within the `Derive` function of `CExtKey` to reject indices that exceed the `2^32 - 1` limit, thus preventing cryptographic weakness or re-derivation of previously used paths.

prs.description: [24.x] Bump version to 24.0rc3
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the Bitcoin Core version number to 24.0rc3, signifying a step closer to the final 24.0 release. This indicates the software is undergoing final testing before a stable release.
prs.technical_summary: This pull request performs a version bump within the Bitcoin Core codebase, specifically updating the version string to '24.0rc3' for the 24.x development branch. This action is a standard part of the release process for a release candidate, marking a snapshot of the code that has undergone significant testing and is nearing its stable release. It involves modifying `configure.ac` and other relevant build configuration files to reflect the new version identifier.

prs.description: p2p: skip querying dns seeds if `-onlynet` disables IPv4 and IPv6
prs.author: mzumsande
prs.public_summary: This PR optimizes network startup by preventing Bitcoin Core from querying DNS seeds if both IPv4 and IPv6 are explicitly disabled. This avoids unnecessary network requests and speeds up node initialization in specific network configurations.
prs.technical_summary: This change modifies the peer-to-peer (P2P) network discovery logic, specifically how DNS seeds are utilized. When the `-onlynet` configuration option is used to disable both `ipv4` and `ipv6`, the code now includes a check to bypass DNS seed queries entirely. This prevents the node from attempting to resolve seed names that would yield unusable addresses, streamlining startup for users operating on alternative network transports like I2P.

prs.description: doc requirement that replacement must have higher feerate than direct conflicts
prs.author: glozow
prs.public_summary: This PR clarifies documentation regarding transaction replacement rules, specifically stating that a replacement transaction must have a higher feerate than its direct conflicts. This provides clearer guidance for developers and users on transaction fee management.
prs.technical_summary: This PR updates the documentation (likely in `policy.md`) to explicitly state the RBF (Replace-By-Fee) policy requirement that a replacement transaction's feerate must exceed that of the transactions it directly conflicts with. This is distinct from the total fee requirement, emphasizing the 'feerate increment' rule for mempool acceptance. The change improves the clarity and precision of the policy specification, which is crucial for wallet developers and service providers interacting with Bitcoin Core's transaction relay policy.

prs.description: build: fix configuring with `--without-experimental-kernel-lib`
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR corrects a build system issue that prevented proper configuration when explicitly disabling an experimental kernel library. This ensures developers can reliably build Bitcoin Core without unwanted experimental features.
prs.technical_summary: The build system's `configure` script is fixed to correctly handle the `--without-experimental-kernel-lib` flag. Previously, this flag could lead to configuration errors. The correction ensures the script properly interprets the directive, avoiding attempts to link or include the experimental library's dependencies, and allows a successful compilation process when disabling this feature.

prs.description: tests: Fix calculation of external input weights
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR corrects how external input weights are calculated in tests, ensuring more accurate and reliable testing of transaction fee estimation and mempool behavior. This fix is crucial for validating transaction construction logic and wallet policies under realistic conditions.
prs.technical_summary: Transaction weight is a critical metric for fee calculation and block inclusion. When testing scenarios with external inputs (e.g., inputs not fully controlled by the testing wallet), their weight contribution must be accurate. This PR addresses a bug in the test framework's calculation logic for these weights, ensuring simulated transactions correctly reflect their true weight and thus improving the precision of tests related to fee estimation and transaction propagation.

prs.description: 23.x backports
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR incorporates a collection of bug fixes, security updates, and minor enhancements specifically into the 23.x release branch. It ensures that the 23.x series remains stable, secure, and up-to-date for its users.
prs.technical_summary: Similar to other release backport PRs, this change involves cherry-picking multiple individual commits from the `master` branch or other stable branches into the `23.x` release branch. The implementation focuses on careful conflict resolution during merges, correct versioning, and thorough verification that all backported changes integrate smoothly without introducing regressions specific to the 23.x series. It serves as a consolidation point for ongoing maintenance.

prs.description: [23.x] Bump version to 23.1rc1
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the internal version number of Bitcoin Core to 23.1 Release Candidate 1, signaling preparation for an upcoming minor release. This is a standard step in the software release cycle, indicating readiness for testing before a stable release.
prs.technical_summary: This change primarily modifies the `VERSION_MAJOR`, `VERSION_MINOR`, and `VERSION_REVISION` macros or constants within the codebase, specifically setting the minor version to `1` and designating it as a release candidate. It is a metadata update reflecting the project's state towards a new stable release branch, typically accompanied by the integration of backported bug fixes and minor improvements from the main development branch into the `23.x` release series. No functional code changes are introduced, only version string modifications for release management.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 23.0.

prs.description: [23.x] qt: Avoid crash on startup if int specified in settings.json
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the stability of the Bitcoin Core GUI by preventing crashes when an integer value is unexpectedly provided in the `settings.json` file. It makes the application more resilient to user-modified or corrupted settings, ensuring a smoother user experience.
prs.technical_summary: This fix targets a specific crash scenario in the Qt GUI where a malformed `settings.json` could lead to an application termination if an integer was parsed where a different data type was expected. The PR implements robust error handling and type checking when reading configuration values from `settings.json`, specifically for the 23.x branch, to gracefully manage invalid input and prevent unexpected application termination.

prs.description: guix: fix GCC 10.3.0 + mingw-w64 setjmp/longjmp issues
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR resolves critical compilation issues within the Guix build system, specifically affecting Windows builds when using GCC 10.3.0. It ensures that Bitcoin Core can be reliably built for Windows targets through our deterministic build process.
prs.technical_summary: The PR rectifies compatibility problems arising from the interaction between GCC 10.3.0, mingw-w64 toolchain, and the `setjmp`/`longjmp` functions used during the Guix build process for Windows. It applies specific patches or adjustments to the build environment or source code to correctly handle these functions' behavior under the given compiler and target, ensuring successful and stable cross-compilation for the Windows platform.

prs.description: net: open p2p connections to nodes that listen on non-default ports
prs.author: vasild
prs.public_summary: This networking enhancement allows Bitcoin Core to establish P2P connections with nodes that are listening on non-default ports. It improves network connectivity and decentralization by enabling wider peer discovery and participation.
prs.technical_summary: Bitcoin nodes typically listen on port 8333. This PR modifies the peer-to-peer networking logic, specifically the address manager and connection establishment routines, to correctly identify and attempt connections to peers advertising non-standard listening ports. This involves adjusting address processing and potentially modifying the connection manager's strategy to correctly interpret and connect to non-default port advertisements, fostering a more robust and flexible peer topology.

prs.description: build: upgrade depends Boost to 1.77.0
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR upgrades the version of the Boost C++ libraries used by Bitcoin Core's dependency build system to 1.77.0. This keeps dependencies current, offering potential performance improvements, bug fixes, and compatibility.
prs.technical_summary: This pull request focuses on updating the `depends` system, which is responsible for building Bitcoin Core's external dependencies, by upgrading the Boost C++ libraries to version 1.77.0. This involves modifying the `depends` scripts and potentially adjusting build configurations to align with any API or build system changes in the new Boost release. Upgrading Boost incorporates performance enhancements, bug fixes, and security improvements from the Boost project, while also ensuring compatibility with modern compiler toolchains and reducing technical debt by maintaining up-to-date core dependencies.

prs.description: Remove -deprecatedrpc=addresses flag and corresponding code/logic
prs.author: mjdietzx
prs.public_summary: This PR removes a previously deprecated configuration flag and its associated code related to RPC addresses. It streamlines the codebase by cleaning up old, unused features, making Bitcoin Core easier to maintain and develop.
prs.technical_summary: This PR removes the `--deprecatedrpc=addresses` command-line flag and all associated logic and code paths from the codebase. This indicates that the functionality controlled by this flag has been fully retired and is no longer supported or necessary. The cleanup involves deleting conditional compilation blocks, configuration parsing, and any RPC handlers or data structures that were part of the deprecated address management system, simplifying the RPC server's architecture.

prs.description: [23.x] macOS / build backports
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR backports essential macOS and build-related fixes and improvements to the 23.x release branch. It ensures that Bitcoin Core builds correctly and runs stably on macOS, enhancing the user experience for Apple users.
prs.technical_summary: This PR integrates a series of patches specifically addressing build system issues and macOS compatibility problems into the 23.x release branch. These backports typically include adjustments to compiler flags, dependency management, or platform-specific API calls to resolve compilation errors or runtime bugs. The changes ensure that automated build processes (e.g., Gitian builds) and local developer setups on macOS function as expected, maintaining cross-platform stability for the release branch.

prs.description: util: Add missing unlinkat to syscall sandbox
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the security of Bitcoin Core by adding the `unlinkat` system call to the application's syscall sandbox. This prevents potential malicious code from deleting files in unexpected ways, bolstering the application's defense against exploits.
prs.technical_summary: Bitcoin Core utilizes a syscall sandbox (e.g., `seccomp` on Linux) to restrict the set of operating system calls the process can execute, thereby minimizing the attack surface. This PR explicitly adds `unlinkat` – a system call for deleting files relative to a directory file descriptor – to the sandbox's allowlist or blocklist. This ensures precise control over file deletion operations within the sandboxed environment, preventing unauthorized or unintended file system modifications.

prs.description: net: fix GetListenPort() to derive the proper port
prs.author: vasild
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a bug in the network code that ensures Bitcoin Core correctly identifies and uses its designated listening port. This is crucial for node connectivity and proper operation, preventing issues where the node might advertise an incorrect port.
prs.technical_summary: This PR targets the `net` (networking) subsystem, specifically correcting the `GetListenPort()` function. The fix addresses an error in the derivation or retrieval logic, ensuring the function accurately returns the port configured for incoming connections, potentially by correcting a variable assignment or logic flow during network initialization.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 22.0.

prs.description: wallet: Reorder locks in dumpwallet to avoid lock order assertion
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR reorders internal locks within the `dumpwallet` function to prevent potential deadlocks or assertion failures. This improves the stability and reliability of the wallet export functionality.
prs.technical_summary: The `dumpwallet` function previously acquired multiple mutexes or locks in an order that could lead to contention issues or deadlock conditions. This change carefully resequences the acquisition of these locks, ensuring a consistent and safe locking hierarchy. By adhering to a strict lock ordering, the PR eliminates race conditions and guarantees the correct execution of wallet dumping operations.

prs.description: build: Perform boost::process detection with BOOST_CPPFLAGS
prs.author: laanwj
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the Bitcoin Core build system's ability to detect `boost::process` correctly across various environments. This ensures more reliable compilation and broader compatibility for the software.
prs.technical_summary: The PR addresses an issue in the build system where `boost::process` detection was unreliable by correctly utilizing `BOOST_CPPFLAGS`. This ensures that necessary preprocessor definitions and include paths are consistently applied during the configure stage, resolving compilation errors that previously occurred due to incorrect Boost library linkage or header discovery.

prs.description: clientversion: No suffix #if CLIENT_VERSION_IS_RELEASE
prs.author: dongcarl
prs.public_summary: This PR modifies how the client version string is generated, ensuring that official release builds do not include development suffixes. This helps in clearly distinguishing stable releases from development snapshots.
prs.technical_summary: This change involves adjusting the preprocessor directives in `src/clientversion.h` or related files. Specifically, it likely wraps the inclusion of version suffixes (e.g., `-rcX`, `-dev`, `(build XX)`) within an `#if !CLIENT_VERSION_IS_RELEASE` block. This ensures that when `CLIENT_VERSION_IS_RELEASE` is defined (for official releases), these suffixes are omitted, resulting in a cleaner and more consistent version string like "0.21.2" instead of "0.21.2-rc1" as reported by the `getnetworkinfo` RPC and GUI.

prs.description: Randomize message processing peer order
prs.author: sipa
prs.public_summary: This PR improves network resilience and privacy by randomizing the order in which messages from connected peers are processed. This helps to mitigate certain types of network attacks and makes it harder for adversaries to infer network topology.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the P2P networking layer's message handling logic. It introduces randomization when selecting which peer's messages to process next, instead of a fixed order. This likely involves shuffling the list of active peers or employing a random selection mechanism before iterating through their message queues, thereby obscuring message propagation patterns.

prs.description: net, rpc: expose high bandwidth mode state via getpeerinfo
prs.author: theStack
prs.public_summary: This feature exposes a peer's 'high bandwidth mode' state through the `getpeerinfo` RPC, providing users and network analysts with more insight into peer capabilities and network behavior. It enhances network diagnostic tools.
prs.technical_summary: The PR extends the JSON output of the `getpeerinfo` RPC call to include a new field indicating whether a connected peer is operating in 'high bandwidth mode'. This mode is typically determined by peer service flags or observed network behavior, like active compact block relay. The networking layer's `CNode` or `CNodeState` objects are updated to track this state, and the RPC handler is modified to query and present this information to the user.

prs.description: wallet: Add missing BlockUntilSyncedToCurrentChain
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances wallet reliability by ensuring that certain operations wait until the wallet is fully synchronized with the current blockchain state. This prevents transactions from being built or broadcast based on outdated information, improving the accuracy of balances and transaction validity.
prs.technical_summary: The change introduces `BlockUntilSyncedToCurrentChain` calls to critical wallet code paths, ensuring that operations like coin selection, transaction creation, or balance queries execute only after the wallet's internal chain tip matches the node's current best chain. This prevents race conditions and stale data issues by blocking execution until the `CWallet`'s internal state reflects the current `ChainActive()` tip. It guarantees a consistent view of the UTXO set and transaction history before proceeding with sensitive wallet operations.

prs.description: [22.x] rc2 backports
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR bundles several backports to the `22.x` release candidate 2 branch. These changes integrate critical fixes and minor improvements, ensuring the stability and readiness of the upcoming 22.x release.
prs.technical_summary: This pull request constitutes a set of cherry-picked commits from the `master` branch, specifically targeting the `22.x` release candidate 2 (rc2) branch. It typically involves applying a curated list of non-controversial bug fixes, performance enhancements, or minor feature updates deemed essential for the stability and quality of the release candidate. Each backported commit is reviewed for compatibility with the `22.x` codebase, and any necessary merge conflicts are resolved to ensure a clean integration without regressions for the pending release.

prs.description: addrman: reset I2P ports in all "new" buckets
prs.author: vasild
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the network address manager's handling of I2P addresses by ensuring that I2P-specific ports are correctly reset. This helps maintain the health and connectivity of the P2P network, especially for I2P nodes.
prs.technical_summary: The `addrman` component needs to properly manage I2P peer addresses, which use distinct port allocation strategies. This PR addresses an issue where I2P ports might not be correctly initialized or reset when an I2P address is moved into a 'new' bucket. The fix modifies the `CAddrInfo` update logic to explicitly reset the I2P port field to zero when a new I2P address entry is created or moved, ensuring proper re-evaluation on subsequent connection attempts.

prs.description: contrib: add torv3 seed nodes for testnet, drop v2 ones
prs.author: laanwj
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the testnet seed nodes to exclusively use Tor v3 addresses, removing the deprecated Tor v2 addresses. It improves the privacy and security of testnet connections for users relying on Tor.
prs.technical_summary: This contribution updates the hardcoded seed nodes specifically for the Bitcoin testnet within the `contrib` directory. It involves adding new Tor v3 onion service addresses, which are longer and provide enhanced cryptography, to the list. Simultaneously, it removes all entries for the older, less secure Tor v2 onion services. This change ensures that testnet nodes connecting via Tor use the latest protocol version, aligning with the broader Tor network's deprecation of v2 services and improving the robustness of peer discovery over Tor.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.21.2.

prs.description: [0.21] Backport: Reset scantxoutset progress before inferring descriptors
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR, a backport for version 0.21, ensures accurate wallet descriptor inference by resetting the scantxoutset progress. This prevents potential issues where previous scan states could lead to incorrect or incomplete descriptor generation.
prs.technical_summary: Wallet descriptors are used to describe sets of UTXOs for a wallet, and `scantxoutset` is a process to find these. Before inferring descriptors, it's crucial to have a clean state to ensure reliability. This PR ensures that any in-progress or residual state from a prior `scantxoutset` operation is cleared, guaranteeing that descriptor inference starts with a fresh scan and produces correct results for wallet management.

prs.description: [0.21] gitian: Use custom MacOS code signing tool
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This update improves the reproducible build process for Bitcoin Core on macOS by implementing a custom code signing tool. This ensures the integrity and authenticity of Bitcoin Core executables distributed for Apple systems.
prs.technical_summary: This pull request integrates a custom macOS code signing utility into the Gitian build process for the 0.21 release branch. Traditionally, macOS code signing can introduce non-determinism due to reliance on specific system tools or certificates. The custom tool aims to provide a more controlled and reproducible signing step, ensuring that the resulting macOS binaries are properly signed while maintaining Gitian's core principle of bit-for-bit identical builds, thus enhancing the security and verifiable authenticity of the macOS distribution.

prs.description: [0.21] qt: Pre-0.21.2rc2 translations update
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the translations for the Bitcoin Core graphical user interface (GUI) ahead of the 0.21.2 release candidate. It ensures that the software is more accessible and user-friendly for non-English speakers.
prs.technical_summary: This involves pulling in updated `.ts` (translation source) files, typically generated from Transifex or a similar localization platform, and recompiling the `.qm` (Qt message) files. These updates reflect string changes, new features, or corrections made since the last translation snapshot for the Qt GUI, ensuring the latest localized text is available for the upcoming release. The `lupdate` and `lrelease` tools are used in the build process.

prs.description: [0.21] Introduce DeferredSignatureChecker and have SignatureExtractorClass subclass it
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces `DeferredSignatureChecker`, a new mechanism that improves the flexibility and efficiency of signature validation within Bitcoin Core. It enables more advanced and potentially asynchronous signature verification strategies, benefiting future script developments and performance optimizations.
prs.technical_summary: `DeferredSignatureChecker` is introduced as a new abstract base class or interface, designed to allow signature verification operations to be queued or processed at a later, more opportune time. The `SignatureExtractorClass`, which is likely responsible for parsing and preparing signatures from transaction scripts, is updated to subclass this new deferred checker. This architectural refactoring enables a more decoupled approach to signature validation, potentially allowing for batch processing of cryptographic checks or improved resource management during transaction evaluation, thereby enhancing throughput and extensibility.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.21.0.

prs.description: [backport] build: Avoid secp256k1.h include from system
prs.author: dergoegge
prs.public_summary: This backport PR improves the build system by preventing Bitcoin Core from accidentally including a system-wide `secp256k1.h` header. This ensures that the correct, bundled version of the cryptographic library is always used, avoiding potential build issues or runtime inconsistencies.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the `depends` build system or the main project's CMake/autotools configuration to explicitly prioritize the vendored `secp256k1` library header (`secp256k1.h`) over any system-installed versions. This is typically achieved by adjusting include paths or compiler flags to ensure `-I/path/to/local/secp256k1` takes precedence. The change prevents potential ABI mismatches or build failures that could arise from using an incompatible `secp256k1` header.

prs.description: test: Fix intermittent issue in mempool_compatibility
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR resolves an intermittent test failure related to the mempool's compatibility with various transaction types. This improves the reliability of our automated tests, ensuring the mempool behaves as expected under all conditions.
prs.technical_summary: This PR addresses an intermittent failure observed in the `mempool_compatibility` test suite. The issue likely stemmed from timing-sensitive interactions or specific transaction relay sequences that, under certain test execution conditions, led to non-deterministic outcomes. The fix identifies and rectifies the root cause, possibly through improved synchronization mechanisms, stricter transaction ordering within tests, or adjusted timeouts, thereby enhancing the determinism and stability of mempool-related integration tests without altering core mempool logic.

prs.description: P2P: Mempool tracks locally submitted transactions to improve wallet privacy
prs.author: amitiuttarwar
prs.public_summary: This PR significantly improves wallet privacy by enabling the node's mempool to track transactions submitted by the local wallet separately from those received from peers. This prevents locally generated transactions from being easily linked to the originating node through standard mempool queries.
prs.technical_summary: The implementation introduces a new attribute or flag within the mempool's transaction data structure to mark transactions that originate from the local node via RPCs like `sendrawtransaction`. When RPC calls such as `getmempoolentry` or `getrawmempool` are executed, they now filter out these 'local' transactions by default, unless explicitly requested. This creates a logical partition in mempool visibility, making it harder for network observers to correlate specific transactions with the user's node, thereby bolstering privacy without affecting global transaction propagation.

prs.description: qt: Pre-splitoff translations update
prs.author: laanwj
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the graphical user interface (GUI) translations for Bitcoin Core, preparing for a future modularization of the translation process. It improves the user experience for non-English speakers by ensuring the application text is up-to-date and accurate.
prs.technical_summary: This PR incorporates the latest translations for the Qt GUI, specifically in preparation for a 'splitoff' of the translation infrastructure. It likely involves merging updated `.ts` (Qt Linguist translation source) files, which will be compiled into `.qm` (Qt message) files. The 'pre-splitoff' suggests a refactoring effort is underway to make the translation system more independent or easier to manage, making this an intermediary update before that larger architectural change.

prs.description: wallet: fix potential division by 0 in WalletLogPrintf
prs.author: jonasschnelli
prs.public_summary: This PR resolves a potential bug in the wallet's logging function that could lead to a crash if certain values were zero. It improves the robustness of the wallet by preventing division-by-zero errors in its internal diagnostics.
prs.technical_summary: This PR introduces a check to prevent a division-by-zero error in the `WalletLogPrintf` function, specifically when calculating rates or percentages. It likely involves adding a conditional guard (e.g., `if (denominator != 0)`) before performing a division operation. This ensures the logger gracefully handles edge cases where a divisor might unexpectedly be zero, preventing application crashes and improving the stability of wallet-related diagnostic output.

prs.description: doc: Move 0.21.0 release notes from wiki
prs.author: laanwj
prs.public_summary: This PR migrates the official release notes for Bitcoin Core version 0.21.0 from an external wiki to the project's repository. This ensures that release information is more accessible and consistently versioned alongside the code.
prs.technical_summary: This change involves transferring the content of the 0.21.0 release notes from an external MediaWiki instance into a dedicated documentation file within the Bitcoin Core repository. The existing documentation structure will be updated to reference this new internal file. This centralizes release information and improves maintainability by integrating it into the standard Git workflow, enhancing discoverability and reducing reliance on external documentation platforms.

prs.description: build: Drop make dist in gitian builds
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR streamlines the Gitian build process by removing an unnecessary `make dist` step. This optimizes build times and reduces complexity for creating reproducible Bitcoin Core binaries.
prs.technical_summary: This PR removes the `make dist` target execution from the Gitian build scripts. The `make dist` command is typically used to create a source tarball for distribution, but in the context of Gitian builds, the source is already directly pulled from Git. Eliminating this redundant step reduces disk I/O, saves CPU cycles, and simplifies the build manifest, leading to faster and more efficient reproducible builds without altering the final binary artifacts.

prs.description: build: replace libdmg and genisoimage with xorriso
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR streamlines the build process for macOS release artifacts by replacing `libdmg` and `genisoimage` with `xorriso`. This improves maintainability and simplifies the dependency stack for creating disk images.
prs.technical_summary: The build system's reliance on external utilities `libdmg` and `genisoimage` for creating macOS `.dmg` and generic `.iso` release packages is replaced by the more modern `xorriso` tool. This refactoring standardizes the creation of ISO 9660 filesystems and DMGs, which simplifies build scripts, reduces the number of external dependencies, and enhances cross-platform build consistency.

prs.description: rpc: deprecate banscore field in getpeerinfo
prs.author: jonatack
prs.public_summary: This PR deprecates the 'banscore' field in the `getpeerinfo` RPC command. This change helps streamline the RPC interface by removing a less-used or potentially misleading field, preparing for future API improvements and reducing client-side complexity.
prs.technical_summary: The implementation involves marking the `banscore` field as deprecated within the `getpeerinfo` RPC method definition. While the field might still be present for a transition period, callers are advised to no longer rely on it. This signals a future removal, guiding RPC client developers to adapt their integrations.

prs.description: Bugfix: RPC/Wallet: Make BTC/kB and sat/B fee modes work sanely
prs.author: luke-jr
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a bug in the RPC and Wallet components to ensure that fee rates specified in 'BTC/kB' and 'sat/B' are calculated and applied correctly. This makes transaction fee estimation more reliable and predictable for users and applications using these units.
prs.technical_summary: This PR targets the `RPC` and `Wallet` subsystems, specifically correcting the logic for parsing and applying transaction fee rates. The fix addresses erroneous calculations or conversions when fees are provided in `BTC/kB` or `sat/B` units, ensuring the wallet accurately interprets these values and derives the correct fee amount for transactions, likely involving adjustments to unit conversion factors.

prs.description: build: add stack-clash and control-flow protection options to hardening flags
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This build system improvement adds modern compiler hardening flags to protect Bitcoin Core executables against sophisticated memory-corruption attacks like stack-clash and control-flow exploits. It significantly enhances the security posture of running nodes.
prs.technical_summary: The PR modifies the build configuration (e.g., `configure.ac` and `Makefile.am`) to enable specific compiler flags such as `-fstack-protector-strong` and control-flow integrity (CFI) options (e.g., `-fcf-protection=full`). These flags instruct the compiler to insert runtime checks and generate more secure code, making it substantially harder for attackers to exploit buffer overflows or hijack program execution flow, thereby mitigating common classes of software vulnerabilities.

prs.description: wallet: fix change detection of imported internal descriptors
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a bug where the wallet failed to correctly detect change outputs for addresses derived from imported internal descriptors. This ensures that funds sent as change to these addresses are properly recognized and accounted for in the wallet balance.
prs.technical_summary: When importing a descriptor wallet that uses internal descriptors for change addresses, the existing wallet logic had an oversight in matching change outputs back to these specific descriptor types. This PR targets the `IsChange()` method within `CWallet`'s transaction scanning. It ensures that the derivation path and script type associated with an output correctly map to the imported internal descriptor for change, thereby accurately identifying and confirming internal change addresses.

prs.description: [wip] build: Switch from C++11 to C++17
prs.author: practicalswift
prs.public_summary: This work-in-progress Pull Request initiates the upgrade of Bitcoin Core's codebase from the C++11 standard to C++17. This modernizes the build environment, allowing developers to leverage new language features for improved performance, safety, and maintainability.
prs.technical_summary: Migrating a large codebase from C++11 to C++17 involves updating compiler flags, build system configurations (e.g., `configure.ac`, `Makefile.am`), and potentially refactoring code. This PR would involve initial changes to `AM_CXXFLAGS` or `CXXSTD` variables, enabling C++17 features, and addressing any immediate compilation errors or warnings. The benefits include access to `std::optional`, `std::variant`, `std::filesystem`, and other C++17 features that can simplify code and improve type safety.

prs.description: Fix locking on WSL using flock instead of fcntl
prs.author: meshcollider
prs.public_summary: This PR resolves an issue with file locking on Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) by switching from `fcntl` to `flock` for file locking. This ensures correct and reliable operation of Bitcoin Core when run in WSL environments.
prs.technical_summary: File locking is critical for preventing data corruption from multiple Bitcoin Core instances. On Linux, `fcntl` and `flock` are used for file locking, but they behave differently, especially in environments like WSL. This PR identified that `fcntl` locks behave unreliably in WSL, likely due to how WSL's kernel compatibility layer translates system calls. Switching to `flock` provides a more robust and consistently behaving locking mechanism under WSL, ensuring mutual exclusion for critical files such as `debug.log` or the wallet lock file.

prs.description: qt: Add missing QPainterPath include
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a build issue in the Qt user interface by adding a necessary header file, ensuring the graphical interface compiles correctly. This resolves a compilation error and improves the reliability of the build process for GUI components.
prs.technical_summary: This PR is a build system or code fix specific to the `qt` (graphical user interface) component. It addresses a compilation error by adding `#include <QPainterPath>` to one or more source files where the `QPainterPath` class was used but its header was not explicitly included, resolving an 'undefined symbol' error during the build.

prs.description: [0.20] Fix GBT: Restore "!segwit" and "csv" to "rules" key
prs.author: luke-jr
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a bug in the GetBlockTemplate (GBT) RPC by restoring the "rules" key to correctly include `!segwit` and `csv` (CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY) when applicable. This ensures mining pools using GBT receive accurate information about consensus rules, preventing block rejections due to outdated templates.
prs.technical_summary: GetBlockTemplate (GBT) is an RPC method used by miners to construct new blocks. The `rules` field in the GBT response indicates the consensus rules active on the network. This bug meant that `!segwit` and `csv` were erroneously omitted. The fix involves correcting the logic within the `getblocktemplate` RPC implementation to always include these rules in the `rules` array when they are relevant for block validity, ensuring miners receive a complete and correct set of rules for constructing valid blocks.
